liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Help On The Way** (2 reviews): The Help on the Way>Slipknot!>Franklin's Tower opener is singled out as an all-time great version; The Help>Slipknot>Franklin's opener is described as on fire [8][9]
- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): Reviewer mentions a bluesy 'Blind Man' passage as some of the best bluesy playing, though no such song is on the setlist [12]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Peggy-O is called perfect, with a flawless mix and sound quality [17]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): The Music Never Stopped is called one of the all-time great versions [8]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Bertha's tempo is considered a little slow, though other highlights make up for it [18]
- **Comes A Time** (1 review): The second-set Comes A Time is described as otherworldly, one of the reviewer's favorite Jerry moments [8]

## The recordings

- **gd77-05-09.sbd.connor.8304.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 178 min; rated 4.86/5 by 141 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound is praised as well in tune, with notes that resonate clearly; Reviewer calls the Betty Cantor board sound quality unbeatable [12][18]
- **gd1977-05-09.sbd.painoman.77462.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 158 min; rated 4.9/5 by 10 [5]
- **gd77-05-09.aud.maizner.vernon.8036.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 163 min; rated 4.56/5 by 25 [7]. Said about its sound: The audience recording is described as very good quality, rivaling the soundboard while giving a feeling of being in the crowd [16]
- **gd1977-05-09.mtx.seamons.98168.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 177 min; rated 4.67/5 by 24 [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer's first show, attended at age 14 when a brother brought them along with a spare ticket [14]
- Reviewer thinks this show may be the high point of May 1977 [8]
- Reviewer recommends it for fans of the Keith and Donna era of the band [11]
- Reviewer suggests the audience version is a worthwhile alternative to the commonly heard soundboard [16]
- Reviewer says it holds its own against the best of the East Coast May tour [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd77-05-09.sbd.connor.8304.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard with patches from Audience [1]. Also: Soundboard from Betty Cantor's two-track 7.5 ips reel with DBX-1, transferred through a PCM501ES, with DBX decoding [1]
- **gd1977-05-09.sbd.painoman.77462.shnf**: transferred by Chris Paino; source: SBD>REEL>PCM>DAT>CDR [5]. Also: Transfer had clicks removed between Slipknot and Franklin's, Bertha and Good Lovin', before Ship of Fools, and Estimated and Other One [5]
- **gd77-05-09.aud.maizner.vernon.8036.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Steve Maizner; source: Audience Recording: Sony ECM-33Ps [7]
- **gd1977-05-09.mtx.seamons.98168.flac16**: source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Pete Mason: [Grateful Dead May 9, 1977 show at Buffalo Memorial Auditorium stands toe to toe with Barton Hall](https://nysmusic.com/2023/05/09/grateful-deads-5-9-77-show-at-buffalo-memorial-auditorium-stands-toe-to-toe-with-barton-hall/) [21]
- Fan art by buffalofm.wnymedia.net: [ANNIVERSARY: Grateful Dead @ Memorial Auditorium 5.9.77 | Buffalo.fm](https://buffalofm.wnymedia.net/2019/05/08/anniversary-grateful-dead-the-aud-5-9-77/) [22]
- Fan art by Allformusic: [Écouter 1977-05-09: War Memorial Auditorium, Buffalo, NY, USA - Grateful Dead | Streaming gratuit](https://www.allformusic.fr/albums/b2a2a2f5-7974-4c67-bf21-f08c28a71eaa) [23]
